issues.description: The problem statement and tests refer to a function named make_y_state(circ, q, p) but the template repository defines a stub named create_y_state(...) instead (and its NotImplemented message even references make_y_state). This name mismatch is structural: students following the instructions will implement make_y_state but the template does not provide that symbol, causing confusion or import/runtime errors. The solution repository implements make_y_state, so the intended name is make_y_state.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the stub in the template from create_y_state to make_y_state and ensure the signature matches the problem statement (make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None). Update any docstrings/comments that reference the old name so all artifacts consistently use make_y_state.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a function named make_y_state(...) to prepare a noisy |Y> ancilla, but the template declares this stub as create_y_state(...). This naming mismatch will confuse students and cause tests to look for make_y_state while the starter code exposes create_y_state.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template stub create_y_state(...) to make_y_state(...), and update its docstring / error message to reference make_y_state so the template, problem statement, and solution use the same identifier.
